purpose: Evidence for the project owner to sign off, or not, on thirteen more candidate events for Milestone 1: eleven that bring the recorded eligible total to the 20-event target, and two spares. Nothing here is an acceptance: each event stays quarantined, and no label is computed, until attestations are added.
how_candidates_were_chosen: From the 110 frozen candidates with no review flags, using only SEC filing metadata and wire pages: 8-K acceptance time, a clean 8-K neighbourhood, common stock on Nasdaq or NYSE, and a wire release with a minute stamp (Business Wire, GlobeNewswire or PR Newswire). Sixteen were dry-run; all sixteen had every session, no zero-volume day and no corporate action in any window. Thirteen are proposed by an outcome-blind rule: the eleven with no 8-K inside their window, plus the two whose only in-window 8-Ks are Item 5.02 (OKTA, REAL) as a two-event margin. Three others are held in reserve. No price or return data was viewed.
target_arithmetic: Recorded eligible events today: 9 across 9 issuers. The eleven core candidates would make 20 across 20 issuers, exactly the target of 20 events across 15 issuers; the two spares add margin.

dry_run.result: Sixteen pending events ran with no attestations: every event quarantined on FIRST_PUBLIC_TIME_UNVERIFIED with no labels, no missing session, no zero-volume day and no corporate action. The ten recorded events again matched their pinned digests.

signoff_items_requested.first_public_time_and_historical_identit: Accept the chronology and identity evidence per candidate, including the residual gap that open-web search cannot close.
signoff_items_requested.corporate_actions: Accept two independent clean signals per candidate: no Item 3.03/5.03 8-K, and Alpaca's real, fully paginated corporate-actions response empty for the window.
signoff_items_requested.provider_rights_at_the_new_scale: Recorded events would grow from 10 to 23. On 2026-09-26 the batch of eight proceeded under the standing 2026-09-23 authorization without your separately addressing the aggregate-at-scale question. Please answer it explicitly this time: is the authorization (derived ratios, booleans, counts and hashes only, never raw prices) still fine at about twenty-three events?
